_purpose: WBS 5.2 synthetic narrative corpus for free-text redaction rules v0.1 (docs/development/revitalise-redaction-rules.md). SYNTHETIC ONLY: every name, practice, address, phone number and email is invented. Phone numbers are from Ofcom's reserved drama ranges (07700 900xxx, 0113 496 0xxx, 020 7946 0xxx); emails use example.org/example.com. Nothing here was taken from docs/Import/ or any real application.
_markup: [[CATEGORY:text]] marks a gold span. CATEGORY is one of NAME, FAMILY MEMBER, GP PRACTICE, ADDRESS, PHONE, EMAIL, AGE. The plain text is the narrative with the markup removed. `expected` is the redacted output the rules require, written out by hand; test_redaction_reference.py checks it agrees with the gold spans, so a hand-typing slip fails the suite.
_simulated_ai: For the logic tests only, a 'perfect' prebuilt model is simulated: every gold NAME and FAMILY MEMBER span becomes a PersonName entity, GP PRACTICE an Organization entity, AGE an Age entity, at `ai_score` (default 0.93). ADDRESS, PHONE and EMAIL are NOT simulated, because the prebuilt model is documented as US-format only - the deterministic rules must find them. `ai_extra` adds further simulated entities (overlaps, retained types, low scores) by value and occurrence. A LIVE run replaces all of this with the model's real output (score_live_run.py).

_rev20: TAD rev 20, ADR-073: postcodes written without their space and districts on their own, confirmed against the postcode register (provisioning/dataverse/data/city-settlement-register.csv, the seed script's source). Kept apart from `samples` because the v0.1 regex specification predates the register. SYNTHETIC: districts are public postcode areas, not anyone's address. `ai_entities` is the simulated extractor's whole answer (none here: the register and shapes own these spans). `expected_reasons` are the column reason kinds (residual-<kind>) with the register available.
